text:
A failed cooling pump caused the outage at the Ruvenna data centre last spring, according to an official review.

The outage began at 02:14 on 17 April, after the primary cooling pump in Hall C stopped working. Temperatures in the hall rose from 22°C to 38°C in 41 minutes, forcing an automatic shutdown of 312 server racks.

The findings appear in Incident Review IR-2217, issued by the Ruvenna Infrastructure Authority on 9 May.

Tomasz Velkarin, facilities operations lead at the Ruvenna data centre, confirmed the pump failure to staff the same morning.

"The primary pump in Hall C stopped working, and the heat built up faster than the systems could cope with," Velkarin said.

The review identifies the pump failure as the cause of the shutdown. The automatic shutdown of the racks was triggered by the rising temperatures in Hall C.
